newsitem.title: USA: Chicago, Southwest plan $722 mln airport expansion.
newsitem.headline: Chicago, Southwest plan $722 mln airport expansion.

text.p: With the backing of Southwest Airlines, Chicago plans a $722 million expansion of its Midway Airport, city officials announced Tuesday.

Mayor Richard Daley, joined by Southwest chairman and chief executive officer Herb Kelleher, said the city has the airline's financial committment for a new terminal building, expanded concourses, a new parking facility and other improvements.
The city last week sold $254 million of general airport revenue bonds backed by Southwest landing fees and terminal rents for the project, Daley said.

The rest of the $722 million project will be funded through additional bond sales backed by airport revenues, as well as federal aviation monies and Midway's passenger facility charge revenues, according to Mary Rose Loney, Chicago's aviation commissioner.

Ron Repel, the city's deputy aviation commissioner, said that because Southwest accounts for about 50 percent of the activity at Midway, the airline was expected to pay 50 percent of the costs of the project.
He added that a subsequent bond issue for Midway probably would not be sold until late 1998.
The deal with Southwest also affords both the city and the airline protection against possible encrouchment by state of Illinois officials into the city's airports.
Kelleher said the airline has the option to leave Midway should there be a successful attempt to wrest control of the airport from Chicago or to redirect airport funds away from the airport itself.
"Southwest is in the position to say we're leaving and you owe us for all the money we invested," Kelleher said.
Last year, Republicans in the Illinois General Assembly unsuccessfully tried to create a state-dominated authority to own and control Chicago's airports.

The move ignited fears on the part of the Daley Adminstration that Republican lawmakers wanted to siphon revenues from Midway and O'Hare International airports to help finance a $2.3 billion airport Gov. Jim Edgar wants to build in Peotone, a town about 35 miles southwest of Chicago.
Both Daley and Kelleher said they doubted Edgar would be able to line up financing for the Peotone airport project, which the major airlines, including Southwest, are on record as opposing.

The Midway expansion project, scheduled to begin in the spring and end by late 2002 or early 2003, will increase terminal and concourse space by 252 percent. Statistics provided by Chicago showed that the number of jet aircraft gates would grow to 38 from 28 and annual passenger enplanements would increase to 8.5 million from 6.6 million.
Kelleher said the terminal expansion would greatly allow his airline to expand number of daily departures beyond the current 97.
While he did not rule out adding destinations from Midway to east coast cities if the airline could be accomodated at airports there, he declined to be specific about new destinations.
